api:
<HrDiagram data={stars} temperature={|s: &Star| s.kelvin} luminosity={|s: &Star| s.luminosity} radius={|s: &Star| s.radius} />
PropTypeDefault
datarequired
temperatureFn(&T) -> f64: surface temperature in kelvinrequired
luminosityFn(&T) -> f64: in solar luminositiesrequired
radiusFn(&T) -> f64: sizes each starone size
point_sizef326.
tooltip, class

Both axes are logarithmic and temperature runs hot to cool, left to right, as astronomers draw it. Each star is coloured by its temperature, from red through white to blue.

examples.title: Stars
examples.description: Hot stars on the left, bright stars on top, coloured by temperature: main sequence, giants and white dwarfs.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn sky() {
    let data = use_signal(stars());
    rsx! { <HrDiagram data={data} temperature={|s: &Star| s.kelvin} luminosity={|s: &Star| s.luminosity} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Main sequence
examples.description: Only the diagonal band of hydrogen-burning stars.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn main_sequence() {
    let data = use_signal(stars().into_iter().take(250).collect::<Vec<_>>());
    rsx! { <HrDiagram data={data} temperature={|s: &Star| s.kelvin} luminosity={|s: &Star| s.luminosity} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: White dwarfs
examples.description: Hot but faint remnants below the main sequence.
examples.code:

examples.title: Cool stars
examples.code:
#[component]
fn cool_stars() {
    let data = use_signal(
        stars()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|s| s.kelvin < 5000.)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <HrDiagram data={data} temperature={|s: &Star| s.kelvin} luminosity={|s: &Star| s.luminosity} class="h-96" /> }
}
